column1: IR Patient Tracker - Instructions
Normal Google Sheet - no script, no permission prompts. Share it freely.
Tabs in this workbook
Settings        = add new Procedure Types, Operators, Referring Doctors, or Payer
Schemes here. They automatically appear as dropdowns everywhere else.
Patient Log     = enter one row per patient/procedure here.
Patient Lookup  = type a UHID, see that patient's full record as a single card -
no scrolling needed.
Analytics       = auto-calculated, filterable dashboard. Do not type here except
the four yellow filter cells at the top.
Adding a new Procedure Type / Operator / Referring Doctor / Payer Scheme
Go to Settings and type the new name into the next blank row of the relevant
table. For a new Procedure Type, also fill its default Follow-up Type/Interval -
this becomes the 'Suggested Follow-up' shown in Patient Log whenever that
procedure is selected. It's a suggestion only; you still type the actual interval
into Patient Log yourself (so you can override it per patient when needed).
Each Settings table has spare blank rows built in for future growth, and each
Analytics chart already covers that full range, so new entries appear in the
charts automatically - no need to edit Analytics.
Making the sheet feel narrower
Patient Log columns are grouped into sections (Demographics / Procedure / Safety
Labs / Follow-up / Outcome / Admin). Small [-] buttons appear above the column
headers - click one to collapse a section you don't need to see right now.
UHID and Patient Name stay frozen on the left so you always know which row
you're looking at, however far right you scroll.
Avoiding duplicate patient entries
If the same UHID is typed into more than one row, both rows turn orange in the
UHID column - a quick visual check before you assume it's a new patient.
Using the Analytics filters
Change Year / Month / Procedure Type / Operator at the top of Analytics - every
KPI and chart on the page recalculates to match. Leave any of them on 'All' to
ignore that filter. The Monthly Volume trend and Currently Admitted list always
show real-time/trailing data regardless of the Year/Month filters (noted on
each chart) since they are inherently time-based or live views.
Follow-up Status logic (automatic)
Overdue = due date passed, not done (red). Due Soon = due within 7 days
(yellow). Done = 'Follow-up Done Date' filled (green). Pending = due date more
than 7 days away. Not Required = Patient Status is Lost to Follow-up / Expired /
Follow-up Complete.
Using this for a paper or audit
Technical Success, Clinical Outcome, Complication, and Histopathology are
dropdowns, not free text - filter Analytics to your date range/procedure and
screenshot or copy the relevant table straight into your manuscript.
Protecting formula tabs (recommended once in Google Sheets)
Data > Protect sheets and ranges > select 'Analytics' (and optionally 'Settings')
> restrict editing to yourself. Collaborators can still view, just not overwrite
formulas by accident.
